themes.label: Why standard/long-memory models fail to capture volatility stylized facts
themes.need: Someone modeling financial volatility persistence needs to understand why standard GARCH/stochastic-volatility models fail to reproduce long-memory, fat-tail, and scaling stylized facts, and why fractionally-integrated long-memory models are problematic, motivating a simpler component-based alternative.
themes.distributed_justification: The paper's address/affiliation footnote (lines 17-18) interrupts the continuous motivation argument running from the stylized facts through the critique of fractional integration to the alternative component view.

themes.label: HAR-RV model: notation, Heterogeneous Market Hypothesis motivation, and derivation
themes.need: Someone wants to understand and construct the HAR-RV model: the realized/integrated volatility notation, the Heterogeneous Market Hypothesis economic rationale for a three-component volatility cascade, and the derivation from partial volatilities to the final HAR(3)-RV autoregressive equation.

themes.label: Simulation validation: HAR-RV reproduces long memory, fat tails, self-similarity
themes.need: Someone wants evidence that the simple HAR-RV model, despite having no true long-memory property, reproduces the empirical stylized facts of financial returns (kurtosis/fat-tail decay, volatility persistence, self-similarity) via simulation against real USD/CHF data.

themes.label: Empirical data and realized-volatility estimation methodology
themes.need: Someone wants to know what real financial data (USD/CHF, S&P500, T-Bond futures) and realized-volatility estimation methodology (tick-by-tick, two-scales estimator) underlie the paper's empirical HAR-RV estimation.

themes.label: In-sample HAR(3) OLS estimation and goodness-of-fit vs AR(22)
themes.need: Someone wants the in-sample OLS estimation results of the HAR(3)-RV model across three asset classes, including component significance, market-component-weight interpretation, and whether the HAR restrictions are statistically justified against an unrestricted AR(22).

themes.label: In-sample one-day-ahead forecast performance vs AR/ARFIMA benchmarks
themes.need: Someone wants the in-sample one-day-ahead forecasting accuracy of HAR(3) versus AR(1), AR(3), and ARFIMA(5,d,0) benchmarks, measured via RMSE, MAE, and Mincer-Zarnowitz R2.
themes.distributed_justification: Figure 8's caption (showing in-sample HAR predictions/residuals) is interposed within the out-of-sample setup text; it documents the same in-sample forecast-evaluation need as the surrounding prose and Table 4.

themes.label: Out-of-sample forecast performance across horizons
themes.need: Someone wants the out-of-sample forecasting performance of HAR(3) against AR(1), AR(3), and ARFIMA(5,d,0) at 1-day, 1-week, and 2-week horizons, including why short-memory models fail at longer horizons and how HAR(3) compares to ARFIMA in accuracy versus implementation simplicity.
themes.distributed_justification: The out-of-sample setup sentence (line 269-270) is cut mid-sentence by the interposed Figure 8 caption (theme t06) and resumes at line 273; Figure 9's raw images (trash 305-324) separate the results discussion from its own caption and the concluding HAR-vs-ARFIMA comparison.

themes.label: HAR-RV extensibility: jump measures and leverage effects as added regressors
themes.need: Someone building on the HAR-RV framework needs pointers on extending it with additional explanatory variables, separately-measured jump components and leverage effects, as extra regressors.

unassigned.reason: Pure recap paragraph restating findings already established elsewhere: long-memory reproduction (t03), parsimonious structure (t02), and the HAR-vs-ARFIMA out-of-sample simplicity/accuracy tradeoff (t07); no new standalone need beyond those themes.
